A circuit clerk fee plus an ISP processing fee, both county-collected. ISP charges nothing to file a petition and $60 to process a court order. County totals commonly run from roughly $60 to $235; McLean County publishes $136, comprising a $60 filing fee, a $60 state police fee and $16 for four certified copies. Treat every figure as county-specific.

Docket fee $176 under K.S.A. 21-6614(g)(2). The supreme court may additionally impose a charge not exceeding $19 per case to fund non-judicial personnel; 2026 Senate Bill 430 carries that authority from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2030. None in this lane. The only fee waiver in K.S.A. 21-6614 is the specialty court waiver at (a)(3). 2026 House Bill 2724, which would have authorised judges to waive the expungement docket fee on a poverty affidavit, died without enactment, so no general poverty-based statutory waiver exists. Some district courts nonetheless accept a poverty affidavit in practice.

No fee is expected. Administrative Order JB-05-26 (A. 3-26), effective 9 March 2026, lists no fee for a criminal post-judgment motion and provides 'Filing a Criminal Action, Traffic Infraction, or Civil Violation: No fee' in both Superior and District Court. The $60 post-judgment motion fee on that schedule is tied by its own terms to M.R. Civ. P. 55(b)(2), 59, 60(b), 62 and 66, which are civil rules, and does not reach a criminal post-judgment motion. Confirm with the clerk and do not promise a refund.

A petition filed with the clerk of the Missouri municipal, associate circuit or circuit court in which the petitioner was charged or found guilty (§ 610.140.2(1)). Every crime sought to be expunged must be in the one petition (§ 610.140.2(2)). FI-05 is filed with it. Whether any circuit rejects the statewide CR360 in favour of a local form is unresolved, which is why the track carries a local-form override and a clerk-contact step.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Three standard fingerprint cards. Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.

requiredBeforeFiling: Obtain Three standard fingerprint cards. Ring a local police department or sheriff's office and ask whether they take fingerprint impressions on standard cards for a court expungement, whether they can do three cards in one visit, what each costs, whether payment must be in cash, and what identification to bring. These are not the same as the fingerprints taken for a Highway Patrol criminal-history search and you do not need to buy a criminal record to get them. One card is filed with the court, one is sent by the clerk to the Missouri Criminal Record Repository with the summons, and one is yours to keep. Start this early: it is a physical dependency people discover too late.
